I have farmed this land 53 years. I do what I did last year, same as my neighbors in the village. My son works in town so I manage most things myself, my wife helps.

My 20 mu — I keep 15 mu on wheat-maize like always, and 5 mu on cotton because the price has been alright and I know how to grow it.

**Wheat (15 mu):** After maize comes off in October, I plow once and drill the wheat. Before sowing I spread 2 bags of compound fertilizer (that 15-15-15 one the dealer sells, 50 jin bag) on each mu. That's about 50 jin per mu of compound. Then in spring when wheat turns green, I top-dress 1 bag of urea per mu — maybe a little more, urea is cheap enough and I don't want thin ears. I water at green-up, at jointing, and at grain-fill — three times from the well. Last year I got about 450 jin per mu, I think this year same. I spray once for aphids when I see them, maybe twice if bad.

**Maize (15 mu):** Right after wheat harvest in June, no till, just drill the maize into the stubble, this is what everyone does now. I use the improved seed from the dealer, Zhengdan type. At knee-high I top-dress 1.5 bags urea per mu. Water twice if the rain doesn't come. Spray once for borers. I get maybe 550 jin per mu.

**Cotton (5 mu):** I plow the cotton field properly in spring, cotton likes loose soil. I use improved Bt seed — the worms are less trouble now but still I spray 6-7 times through summer, cotton is the crop that eats pesticide money. Base fertilizer 2 bags compound per mu, then urea 1 bag per mu at flowering. Water 3 times. I get around 220 jin seed cotton per mu if weather holds.

I spend more on fertilizer than I probably need, but a bad year is a disaster and some extra urea is just a few hundred yuan.
